# SQL

<!-- Generated by bazel run //tools/docs/languages:languages_bin -- --write from sql/lang.json and sql/defs.bzl. Do not edit. -->

This page helps you build, test and check SQL code with rules_dx.

## Quick start

`MODULE.bazel` sits at the root of your repository and lists the Bazel modules, meaning external dependencies, that your project uses. Add `rules_dx` to it:

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

Then let dx set up the rest, as in the [Quickstart](../../README.md#quickstart):

```sh
bazel run @rules_dx//dx/launch:dx -- init --apply
```

For a SQL project, `MODULE.bazel` then looks like this:

```python
module(name = "my_project")

bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

A `BUILD.bazel` file declares targets: the libraries, binaries and tests that Bazel builds. This one is a small SQL package from [`sql/tests/consumer`](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/sql/tests/consumer/BUILD.bazel):

```python
load("@rules_dx//sql:defs.bzl", "sql_library")

sql_library(
    name = "sql",
    srcs = ["query.sql"],
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)
```

Build and test everything. `//...` means every target in the repository:

```sh
tools/dx test //...
```

## Rules

`load` brings rules into a `BUILD.bazel` file. Load the ones you use from `@rules_dx//sql:defs.bzl`:

```python
load("@rules_dx//sql:defs.bzl", "sql_library")
```

### `sql_library`

Owns the SQL files of one package for dx quality.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `srcs` | `label_list` | no | SQL files of this package. |
| `dialect` | `string` | no | SQL dialect of every source; empty lets each file's dialect suffix decide. |
| `deps` | `label_list` | no | SQL libraries this package depends on. |

## Tools and package files

dx runs these tools and reads these package files for SQL:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Tools | `sqlfluff` |
| Ecosystems | none |
| Manifests | none |
| Lockfiles | none |

## Platforms

SQL builds and tests on:

- Linux arm64
- Linux x86_64
- macOS arm64
- Windows x86_64
